work_order.understanding:
Attempt 2's DIAGNOSIS was right and its fix worked: one shared predicate, derived from COMPONENTS, and QA confirmed it — all twelve acceptance criteria pass, the three defects attempt 1 filed are genuinely closed, and the 78-page sweep is clean. I am not rewriting it. What attempt 2 got wrong is narrower and sharper than QA's 'a two-word overclaim in a comment'. The previous work order gave the implementer two instructions that cannot both hold, and then wrote a comment asserting an invariant its own design falsifies.

The first instruction was deliberate and is recorded in its alternatives: 'a stored pSuccess of 1.5 is out of range but is still a number the build can print, so it stays on the wire', pinned by a test named 'a component that is out of range but a real number stays readable' whose stated purpose is to stop 'a future agent' widening the rule into range validation on the read path. The second was the routes.js CONTRACT comment: 'this field is null exactly when one or more of the components in this same body is null.' I reproduced BOTH against df0b3cd, and the comment is false in BOTH directions, not one.

Direction 1 is what QA filed. MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (9007199254740991) is a readable money value and 1.5 is a readable pSuccess under the rule as written, so all eight components project non-null, and expectedContribution's own Number.isSafeInteger guard then returns null because 9007199254740991 x 1.5 is not a safe integer. A second path to null that the comment never accounts for.

Direction 2 is one QA did not find, and it is the reason QA's own suggested fix does not work. The comment quantifies over 'one or more of the components in this same body' — all eight — but expectedContribution reads exactly three: value_micros, pSuccess, cost_micros. A stored record with fit deleted projects {"fit": null} beside expected_contribution_micros 1499000000, which I read off a live HTTP response from the PR branch. So the comment's 'exactly when' is false in the other direction too, and QA's recommended cheapest fix — 'state the contract in one direction only (contribution is null whenever a component is null)' — is a claim that this very record refutes. If this work order took QA's hint literally it would ship a comment that is still wrong, and the next QA run, which has no memory of this one, would file it again.

The honest statement of what went wrong: attempt 2 unified WHICH COMPONENTS ARE READABLE, which was the real duplication, and it did that correctly. It never checked the readability rule against the CLAIM MADE ABOUT IT. The comment specifies a coupling between an eight-key projection and a three-input derived field, and no choice of per-key rule can deliver it, because the formula does not read five of those eight keys. Attempt 2's test suite could not catch this either: the cross-consumer table asserts the four consumers agree about readability, and all four do agree — they simply agree about a question the comment was not asking.

Nothing in the 12 acceptance criteria becomes false under the fix below. I checked each one against the prototype, and AC-8's byte-identical seeded rows hold (opp_seed_expensive projects identically after the change).
work_order.root_cause:
The CONTRACT comment added in src/api/routes.js:367-372 specifies a biconditional between the eight-key component projection and a derived field that reads only three of those eight keys, and the read-side rule it is stated over is deliberately narrower than the domain's own per-key rule. Neither half of the claim can hold, and the two failures are independent.

(a) The comment's clause 'exactly when one or more of the components in this same body is null' quantifies over all eight components, but expectedContribution (src/domain/opportunities.js) guards only value_micros, pSuccess and cost_micros. fit, infoValue, reversibility, downside and delay do not enter trunc(value x p) - cost, so any of those five being null leaves the contribution a number and falsifies the clause. Reproduced: a record with fit deleted returns components.fit === null and expected_contribution_micros 1499000000. No product change can fix this — the formula has no relationship to those five — so the claim, not the code, is what has to change.

(b) The comment asserts that all-eight-non-null implies a number, but isReadableComponent is a number check (money is a non-negative safe integer, every other key merely Number.isFinite) and so deliberately accepts a pSuccess outside [0,1]. With a readable value_micros capped at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, a readable pSuccess of 1.5 makes the product unsafe, and the arithmetic's own Number.isSafeInteger guard then yields a second null the comment never accounts for. This is fixable in code, and it is the half QA filed.

The underlying cause is that 'a component this build can stand behind' and 'a value the domain accepts for this key' are two different rules, and only the first is consulted on the read path. attempt 2 correctly collapsed the first to a single definition across four consumers; it left the second rule — the one validateOpportunity already owns, per key, with its codes and messages — on the write path only. So the read side accepts a value the write side would reject, which is what leaves the contribution's null reachable by a second, unstated route. The defect is the gap between the two rules, not any one of the five sites.
work_order.approach:
Make the contract provable instead of promised, in two parts that fix (b) and (a) respectively.

(1) The read-side rule becomes the domain's own per-key rule. In src/domain/opportunities.js, add one private COMPONENT_RULES table — a single predicate per key, holding exactly the rule validateOpportunity already enforces for that key: the two money keys are non-negative safe integers, pSuccess/fit/reversibility are finite and in [0,1], infoValue/downside/delay are finite and non-negative. isReadableComponent(key, value) becomes COMPONENT_RULES[key]?.(value) === true, so a key with no rule is unreadable by default, and validateOpportunity's three range/money loops delegate their accept-or-reject decision to the same table, keeping every existing error code and message byte-identical (OPP_BAD_MONEY for money, OPP_BAD_COMPONENT for the rest, 'must be between 0 and 1', 'must be non-negative', and the money message naming micros).

COMPONENTS stays the explicit ordered array and the table is keyed in that same order. This is a real trap, not a style note: I first wrote the table as an object literal and took COMPONENTS from Object.keys of it, and the projection's key order changed on the wire — test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js caught it immediately. COMPONENTS order is value_micros, pSuccess, fit, infoValue, reversibility, cost_micros, downside, delay and must survive unchanged.

The consequence, stated plainly because it reverses a boundary attempt 2 documented and deliberately pinned: a stored out-of-range component — pSuccess 1.5, pSuccess -1, fit 2, downside -1 — is now UNREADABLE, so it projects as null, renders as the em-dash, and trips the seed guard. That is the point, not a side effect. A readable pSuccess is then in [0,1] and a readable value_micros is a non-negative safe integer, so trunc(value x p) - cost always lands in [-MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] and IS a safe integer: the arithmetic's own guard becomes unreachable for every record the projection reports as readable. The second null path is removed rather than documented, and the comment's forward implication becomes a theorem instead of a hope. expectedContribution keeps the guard — it is still correct defence for a direct caller that bypasses the projection — but nothing reachable through the wire can trip it.

(2) The CONTRACT comment in src/api/routes.js is rewritten to the invariant that then holds and to nothing more: expected_contribution_micros is null exactly when value_micros, pSuccess or cost_micros is null in this same body; the other five components do not enter the formula, so their nullness never affects it; and the empty case is a number by the arithmetic above. This is comment-only and unavoidable — see root_cause (a). It is a false statement being corrected to a true one, not a criterion being relaxed to match a defect: the code and its tests already agree on this, and the comment is the only thing that disagrees.

(3) The prose that describes the rule in words has to move with it, or it becomes the same defect one layer down. scripts/seed.js:343 tells the operator 'money must be a non-negative integer number of micros and every other component a finite number', and the isReadableComponent doc comment says the same. Both are now false — I watched the seed throw OPP_STALE_RECORD at an operator with a message that misdescribed the rule it was enforcing. Both must describe the range rule instead. The seed message keeps its code, its id, the component-key list and its recovery sentence; only the description of the rule changes.

Not touched, deliberately: src/data/repositories.js (its comment describes the projection correctly as it stands and needs no edit), src/web/pages.js (opportunityRow already reads the projection and renders the em-dash for any null; money() already imports the rule and the money half is unchanged), and docs/** (forbidden).

files.change: Add a private COMPONENT_RULES table beside COMPONENTS, keyed in COMPONENTS order, holding one predicate per key: the two money keys require Number.isSafeInteger && >= 0; pSuccess, fit and reversibility require a finite number in [0,1]; infoValue, downside and delay require a finite number >= 0. Replace the body of isReadableComponent with `COMPONENT_RULES[key]?.(value) === true`, so a key with no rule is unreadable rather than readable. Make validateOpportunity delegate to it: the MONEY_COMPONENTS loop, the RATIO_COMPONENTS loop, the infoValue check and the downside/delay loop each test `!isReadableComponent(key, input[key])` in place of their own inline comparison, keeping every existing error code, field name and message string exactly as they are. Keep COMPONENTS as the explicit ordered array — do NOT derive it from Object.keys(COMPONENT_RULES), which reorders the wire projection. Rewrite the isReadableComponent doc comment: the rule is now the domain's per-key rule, not a number check, so the paragraph that says 'a stored pSuccess of 1.5 is out of range and is still a finite number, so it stays readable' and the one that says it is 'a number check, not a coercion' must both go, replaced by a statement that the read side and the write side are the same rule and that this is what makes the contribution's contract hold.
files.why: This is the whole behavioural change. It removes the second path to a null contribution by making a readable pSuccess in [0,1], which is what turns the routes.js contract from an assertion into a consequence.

files.change: Comment only, no behaviour change, around expected_contribution_micros at src/api/routes.js:379. Replace the CONTRACT comment's biconditional, which currently claims the field 'is null exactly when one or more of the components in this same body is null', with the claim that actually holds after the domain change: the field is null exactly when value_micros, pSuccess or cost_micros is null in this same body, the other five components do not enter the formula and so never affect it, and when all three are readable the result is a number because a readable pSuccess is in [0,1] and a readable value_micros is a non-negative safe integer, so the product cannot leave the safe-integer range. Keep the existing 'null, never 0' paragraph and the stored-record paragraph untouched. Do not leave any wording anywhere in this comment that a client could read as a guarantee about the other five components.
files.why: The comment is a published statement of the wire contract and it is currently false in the direction QA filed. The direction QA did not file cannot be fixed in code at all, because the formula does not read those five components.

files.change: Message text only, no control-flow change. In the OPP_STALE_RECORD message at scripts/seed.js:343, replace the clause 'money must be a non-negative integer number of micros and every other component a finite number' with a description of the rule that now actually runs: money must be a non-negative integer number of micros, the three probability components must be between 0 and 1, and the remaining multipliers must be non-negative. Keep the code, the opportunity id, the unreadable component-key list and the 'delete the database and re-seed' recovery sentence exactly as they are — the existing test/ops/seed.test.js assertions on all of those must still pass unchanged. The import of isReadableOpportunityRecord and unreadableComponents from the domain is already correct and needs no edit; only the prose describing the rule moves.
files.why: I ran the seed against a record with an out-of-range pSuccess and it threw OPP_STALE_RECORD with a message telling the operator the wrong rule, which is the same class of defect as the one this ticket exists to fix.

cases: REPLACE, do not delete, the test named 'a component that is out of range but a real number stays readable'. Its rationale — that the read side must not become a full re-validation — was sound then and is wrong now, and this work order reverses it for a stated reason: a readable pSuccess of 1.5 times a readable MAX_SAFE_INTEGER is what leaves the contribution unrepresentable. The replacement asserts the opposite boundary with equal strength: pSuccess 1.5, pSuccess -1, fit 2 and downside -1 are each unreadable and appear in unreadableComponents, while a pSuccess of exactly 0 and exactly 1 stay readable, so the rule is a closed range and not 'any positive number'. The test name and its comment must record WHY the boundary moved, or the next agent will move it back.

REPLACE, do not delete, the assertion inside 'the rule is a number check, not a coercion' that reads 'a negative multiplier is out of range, not unreadable' and expects true. Keep the rest of that test exactly as it is — the numeric string '2000000000' is unreadable as value_micros, the string '0.5' is unreadable as pSuccess, and null and undefined are unreadable for every key are all still true and are still the coercion guard. Only the out-of-range clause moves, and it moves to the new test above.

ADD the cross-consumer theorem that is the actual regression guard for this attempt, as a table over every existing fixture plus the QA shapes: for each record, assert `expectedContribution(record) === null` if and only if `readableComponents(record)` has value_micros, pSuccess or cost_micros null. Run it over the healthy record, the pre-rename shape, value_micros float 5000000.5, value_micros the string '2000000000', value_micros negative -1000000, pSuccess absent, fit absent, pSuccess the string '0.5', pSuccess 1.5, pSuccess -1, pSuccess 0 and pSuccess 1, and the break-even control. It holds on the fixed code and fails on df0b3cd for the pSuccess 1.5 and pSuccess -1 rows.

KEEP the existing assertion that the projection carries all eight keys in COMPONENTS order, including for the healthy fixture. It is load-bearing in a way this attempt discovered the hard way: deriving COMPONENTS from Object.keys of a rule table reorders the projection on the wire and this assertion is what catches it. Do not relax it to a set comparison or to a length check.

KEEP the existing assertion that unreadableComponents names exactly the keys that are wrong, and that isReadableOpportunityRecord is true for a well-formed record. Both still hold and both now hold for a strictly larger set of corrupt records.

ADD the write-path delegation cases, which are what makes 'one rule' true rather than asserted: for each of the eight keys, at least one value that validateOpportunity accepts and one that it rejects, assert that the verdict matches isReadableComponent for that key on the same value. The rejections to pin are pSuccess -1 and 1.5, fit 2, reversibility -0.1, infoValue -1, downside -1, delay -1, value_micros -1 and 1.5, cost_micros '500000000'; the acceptances are pSuccess 0 and 1, fit 0 and 1, infoValue 0 and 1.2, downside 0, delay 1, and the two valid money values. This is what stops the two paths drifting apart again — attempt 2's AC-12 asked for one definition of readable and this makes it one definition of valid.

KEEP every existing validateOpportunity error-code and message assertion unchanged: OPP_BAD_MONEY for a money value that is a float, a string, a negative or above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; OPP_BAD_COMPONENT for a non-finite or out-of-range non-money component; and the exact message strings. The delegation must not have changed one word of any of them — assert the messages, not just the codes.

KEEP the four tests attempt 1 inverted at the top of this file, and keep the genuine break-even record still returning 0. They pass today and must still pass; they are the guard that distinguishes the unknown (null) from the real zero, which is the distinction the whole ticket rests on.

ADD the boundary case the new rule creates at the arithmetic: with a readable pSuccess of exactly 0 and a readable value_micros of MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, expectedContribution is 0 minus cost_micros, a number; with pSuccess exactly 1 and value_micros MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and cost_micros 0, the contribution is exactly MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, a number and not null. These are the two shapes that prove the previously-unreachable guard is genuinely unreachable rather than merely untested.

REPRODUCE BUG-1 through HTTP, the way QA did, because a domain-level assertion would not have caught it. Plant the stored record from the QA report verbatim: opportunity_id opp_qa_ovf_014, tenant_demo, name 'QA overflow contribution', value_micros 9007199254740991, pSuccess 1.5, fit 0.5, infoValue 1, reversibility 0.9, cost_micros 0, downside 2, delay 1, and a score. Idempotently re-POST a well-formed body over it so the response describes the stored record, then assert components.pSuccess === null AND expected_contribution_micros === null. On df0b3cd this body returns eight non-null components and a null contribution; that is the assertion that failed.

REPRODUCE the second shape QA did not file: plant a record missing only fit, with valid value_micros 3000000000, pSuccess 0.5, cost_micros 1000000 and valid infoValue, reversibility, downside, delay. Re-POST over it and assert components.fit === null AND expected_contribution_micros === 1499000000, and assert that the two money components and pSuccess are all non-null. This is the fixture that makes the corrected comment true and that refutes QA's own suggested one-direction wording, so it must be pinned.

ADD the biconditional as a route-level assertion over the whole corrupt-shape table, not as a comment: for every fixture in the API test file, assert (expected_contribution_micros === null) === (components.value_micros === null || components.pSuccess === null || components.cost_micros === null). One assertion, run per fixture, so a future change cannot satisfy one direction and break the other.

KEEP unchanged the existing healthy-row assertions — the deepEqual on body.components, the eight-key assertion, and the re-post assertion expecting expected_contribution_micros 1_700_000_000 for a well-formed row read back from the stored record. They pass today and AC-8 and AC-2 depend on them.

ADD the seeded-row invariance: a healthy seeded opportunity's projection is byte-identical to its stored record — all eight values equal the stored numbers, none nulled — so that widening the read rule cannot quietly start hiding values the domain accepts.

ADD the shape this attempt makes reachable: plant a seed opportunity whose pSuccess is 1.5, with both money keys valid safe integers and every other component in range. Re-seed and assert the run throws OPP_STALE_RECORD naming pSuccess. It exits 0 on df0b3cd, because a finite out-of-range number was readable there, and it exits non-zero on the fixed code. This is the seed half of the same rule change and the reason the OPP_STALE_RECORD message text has to change with it.
ADD the second out-of-range shape on a different key, so a guard that only knows about pSuccess cannot pass: a record with fit 2, everything else valid, also throws and the message names fit.

UPDATE the assertion that pins the OPP_STALE_RECORD message text. It currently requires the phrase describing the old number-check rule, which is no longer the rule. Generalise it, do not delete it: assert the message names the unreadable component keys, still matches /^OPP_STALE_RECORD/, still contains the opportunity id, still matches /delete the database and re-seed/i, and now also states the range rule for the non-money components. Weakening it to a bare code check is the one thing in this work order that must not happen — the message is the only guidance the operator gets, and this attempt shipped a version of it that described a rule the seed was not running.

KEEP every other seed assertion exactly as it stands: the pre-rename shape still throws, a current-shape database still seeds and re-seeds as a clean idempotent no-op with opportunitiesWritten 0 and alreadySeeded true, and the throw is loud but not atomic. None of these may be relaxed; they are what keeps AC-6 and AC-8 true, and AC-8's byte-identical seeded rows are the check that the widened read rule did not start altering healthy data.
KEEP the assertion that details.unreadable_components names exactly the keys that are wrong, so a guard that throws with a hardcoded field cannot pass.

ADD the view half of the rule change: a stored opportunity with pSuccess 1.5 renders 'success probability —' in that component's slot on /opportunities, not '1.5'. opportunityRow already reads the repository projection and renders the em-dash for any null, so this is a consequence of the domain change rather than a change to pages.js — the test is what stops someone concluding pages.js needs an edit, and what pins the degradation for the browser check in AC-16.
ADD the same for a second key, so the row is not pinned only on pSuccess: a record with downside -1 renders 'downside —'.

KEEP the negative-micros render case ('value —' for value_micros -1000000) and the legacy pre-rename case, including the extension to a record with pSuccess deleted rendering 'success probability —'. Both still hold; the money half of the rule is unchanged by this work order.

KEEP the three grouped-money assertions and the unknown-currency fallback case. This work order makes no change to money() or to currency threading, and no page render may regress while the read rule widens.

acceptance.how_to_verify: node --test test/domain/opportunities.test.js — the absent-money-keys, one-key-missing, non-safe-integer and non-finite-pSuccess cases all read null, and the existing test at :84 is inverted. node --test test/api/opportunities.test.js — the re-POST case asserts null in the response body for a pre-rename row while the existing well-formed re-post at :325 still reads 1_700_000_000.

acceptance.check: Every opportunity row on GET /v1/opportunities carries all eight component keys, and a money component this build cannot read is present-and-null rather than a dropped key. This is a stated wire-format change: a client distinguishing an absent key from an explicit null will see the difference.
acceptance.how_to_verify: node --test test/api/opportunities.test.js — the pre-rename row asserts Object.keys(row.components).length === 8 AND value_micros === null, which fails on today's code (it returns six keys). The qa_script's curl on a healthy seeded database is NOT the check for this: it already returns 8 today and proves nothing about the change.

acceptance.check: Two evaluate calls that land in the same millisecond return appended:false and duplicate:true on the second, and store exactly one evaluation row.
acceptance.how_to_verify: node --test test/api/opportunities.test.js, the clock-frozen route-level test using t.mock.timers.enable({apis:['Date']}) and setTime with a number. QA also POSTs the evaluate endpoint twice in the qa_script and confirms both fields are present on both responses; note for the report that two back-to-back curls normally land in different milliseconds and both say appended:true.

acceptance.check: Money on /opportunities, on /experiments and on the dashboard's Meta regions renders through the repo's currency-aware formatter, thousands-grouped, identically to the Qualified CPL card, and src/web/pages.js contains no second renderer of money.
acceptance.how_to_verify: In the browser on /opportunities, the expensive seeded row reads 'value ₹6,000.00' and 'cost ₹1,900.00' and never '₹6000.00' or a bare 6000000000; on / the ad-set budget reads '₹500.00' and insight spend '₹4,000.00'; on /experiments the caps read '₹500.00' and '₹200.00'. The single-renderer claim is a grep in the review, not a browser check.

acceptance.check: A tenant whose currency is not INR sees its own currency symbol on opportunity value, opportunity cost, the experiment caps and the Meta tables — on the ideal path AND on the meta error/last-good path — and a tenant with an unrecognised currency code still renders instead of throwing.
acceptance.how_to_verify: node --test test/web/pages.test.js, the USD-tenant and unknown-currency cases driven through renderPage. There is deliberately NO browser step, and the honest reason is not the one the first draft gave: a non-INR tenant IS reachable from a CLI (POST a spend event whose currency is USD and src/api/routes.js:158 auto-creates that tenant row), but firstTenant() renders tenants.list()[0] and that query is ORDER BY created_at, id (src/data/repositories.js:27), so a USD tenant created after the demo one is not the tenant the page draws. Seeding a USD-first database would be a browser-reachable path but is out of scope. No existing test pins that ordering and this change does not add one.

acceptance.check: Seeding a database that holds a record this build cannot read fails loudly with a stable code OPP_STALE_RECORD and states the real recovery, instead of reporting a successful no-op.
acceptance.how_to_verify: The qa_script step that seeds a temp DB, plants a pre-rename opp_seed_expensive row with the inlined node one-liner, and re-runs the seed: the command exits non-zero, the message names OPP_STALE_RECORD, opp_seed_expensive and deleting the DB to re-seed, and the 'already present, nothing new written' line never prints. I confirmed the plant-and-reseed sequence reproduces today's silent exit-0 no-op on the unmodified code. node --test test/ops/seed.test.js asserts the same, plus that the second re-seed throws again.

acceptance.check: A malformed, absent or non-integer money value renders '—' on a page rather than '₹NaN' or a 500, and no page render throws on bad tenant or provider data — including an experiment stored with no caps at all.
acceptance.how_to_verify: node --test test/web/pages.test.js — the legacy-row case, the caps-less experiment case, and the unknown-currency case. The '—' guard is the reason this is safe: money() returns '—' for any value that is not a safe integer and never calls fromMicros with one, so a provider or snapshot row carrying a float degrades cosmetically exactly as it does today rather than throwing INVALID_MONEY and 500-ing the whole dashboard.

acceptance.check: Ordinary seeding is unchanged: a fresh database seeds with the same counters, a repeat run is a clean idempotent no-op, and the seeded scores and component values are byte-identical to what the current seed writes.

Note the deliberate behaviour change this carries: the seed's exit code goes from 0 to non-zero on a database it previously reported as seeded. Anything invoking `npm run sdlc:seed` in CI or a dev script will start failing on such a database — that is the intent, and the error message is the only guidance the operator gets.

acceptance.check: An opportunity row whose stored record is missing a NON-money component — pSuccess, fit, infoValue, reversibility, downside or delay — still carries all eight component keys on GET /v1/opportunities, with the missing one explicitly null. acceptance.check: On POST /v1/opportunities, a body whose value_micros, pSuccess and cost_micros are all non-null carries a NUMBER in expected_contribution_micros — including for a stored record whose value_micros is 9007199254740991 (MAX_SAFE_INTEGER) and whose pSuccess is 1.5 or -1, the two shapes in this round's BUG-1. A client that null-checks those three fields and nothing else can rely on the contribution agreeing. The body never presents eight readable components and then an unreadable contribution.
acceptance.how_to_verify: In the qa_script, plant opp_qa_ovf_014 exactly as QA's repro does (direct SQL into the preview SQLite file: value_micros 9007199254740991, pSuccess 1.5, cost_micros 0, all other components valid) and then idempotently re-POST a well-formed body over it so the response describes the stored record. Assert components.pSuccess === null AND expected_contribution_micros === null. Repeat for opp_qa_ovf2_015 (pSuccess -1, cost_micros 1). On the branch this work order replaces, both return all eight components non-null with a null contribution; check the raw body, not a jq projection that could drop the null. node --test test/api/opportunities.test.js holds the same two fixtures at the route level.

acceptance.check: expected_contribution_micros is null EXACTLY WHEN value_micros, pSuccess or cost_micros is null in the same body, in both directions. In particular a component that does not enter the contribution — fit, infoValue, reversibility, downside or delay — being null does NOT and must not null the contribution: a stored record missing only fit projects components.fit === null beside a numeric expected_contribution_micros (1499000000 for the qa_script's fixture). The claim is about those three fields and about no others.
acceptance.how_to_verify: This is the direction QA's own hint got wrong, and it needs its own check because nothing else covers it. In the qa_script, plant a record with fit deleted and otherwise valid components (value_micros 3000000000, pSuccess 0.5, cost_micros 1000000, valid infoValue, reversibility, downside, delay), re-POST a well-formed body over it, and assert components.fit === null while expected_contribution_micros === 1499000000 and the other seven components are non-null. Then read the CONTRACT comment in src/api/routes.js and confirm it claims the biconditional over those THREE fields only. node --test test/api/opportunities.test.js asserts (contribution === null) === (any of the three is null) over the whole fixture table.

acceptance.check: A stored component that is outside the domain's range for its key — pSuccess 1.5, pSuccess -1, fit 2, downside -1, infoValue -1 — is reported as null in components on the wire rather than passed through as its stored value, and makes `npm run sdlc:seed` exit non-zero with OPP_STALE_RECORD naming that key. A value the domain would reject on the way in is not handed back as trustworthy on the way out.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Seed a temp database, plant opp_seed_expensive with pSuccess 1.5 and both money keys valid, re-seed: the command exits non-zero, names OPP_STALE_RECORD and names pSuccess, and the OPP_STALE_RECORD message describes the range rule rather than the old 'every other component a finite number' wording — read the message, it is the operator's only guidance. Same for a record with fit 2. Then re-POST a well-formed body over each and assert the out-of-range component is null in components. A boundary control: pSuccess exactly 0 and exactly 1 are in range and must still be passed through, and every healthy seeded row must still project all eight of its stored values with none nulled (AC-8).

acceptance.check: On /opportunities, a component outside the domain's range for its key renders the em-dash in that component's slot, not the stored number — the same degradation a missing component already gets. A row stored with a pSuccess of 1.5 reads 'success probability —', and a row stored with downside -1 reads 'downside —'. The seeded healthy rows are unaffected: 'success probability 0.6', 'fit 0.9', 'downside 2'.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Plant the out-of-range records from the qa_script, load /opportunities in the browser, and read the row's data-component spans. Also confirm no page returns 5xx and the console stays clean, as in the existing sweep. node --test test/web/pages.test.js holds both renders; note for the report that pages.js itself needs no edit for this — opportunityRow already renders the em-dash for any null the projection returns — so if this criterion fails, the domain change did not take effect rather than the view being wrong.

acceptance.check: The read-side rule and the write-side validation consult the same per-key predicate, so a component the domain would reject on the way in is unreadable on the way out and the two can never be changed independently. This extends AC-12, which asked for one definition of 'readable', to one definition of 'valid': there is no value for which validateOpportunity accepts a key and isReadableComponent rejects it, or the reverse. The projection's key order is unchanged — value_micros, pSuccess, fit, infoValue, reversibility, cost_micros, downside, delay — and a component key cannot be added to the projection without a rule behind it.
acceptance.how_to_verify: node --test test/domain/opportunities.test.js — the per-key delegation table, one accepted and one rejected value for each of the eight keys, asserting validateOpportunity and isReadableComponent reach the same verdict, plus the exact error messages. node --test test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js still asserts all eight keys in COMPONENTS order for every fixture, which is what catches a table that reorders the wire. And the review grep from AC-12 still finds no ad-hoc readability check outside the domain module: with the rule now shared, scripts/seed.js, src/data/repositories.js and src/web/pages.js must contain no per-key range comparison of their own.

qa_script: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run sdlc:seed, then npm run sdlc:serve and wait for /health. All of the planting below goes against a copy of the seeded database, never the preview one, except where a record must be visible to a live HTTP call.

RUN A HEALTHY SEED FIRST AND KEEP THE OUTPUT: npm run sdlc:seed twice, confirming the second run is a clean no-op with opportunitiesWritten 0. This is AC-8 and it is the baseline every other check below is compared against — if the seeded rows differ from what is recorded here, stop and file that, because this change must not alter a single healthy value.

AC-15 SEED CHECK: copy the seeded database to /tmp, and in that copy plant opp_seed_expensive with pSuccess 1.5 and both money keys valid, re-seed against the copy, and confirm the command exits non-zero with OPP_STALE_RECORD naming pSuccess. Then read the message: it must describe the range rule (probability components between 0 and 1, multipliers non-negative) and must NOT still say 'every other component a finite number'. Repeat with fit 2.

AC-13 PLANT AND READ: direct SQL into the preview database, insert opp_qa_ovf_014 for tenant_demo with record {"opportunity_id":"opp_qa_ovf_014","tenant_id":"tenant_demo","name":"QA overflow contribution","value_micros":9007199254740991,"pSuccess":1.5,"fit":0.5,"infoValue":1,"reversibility":0.9,"cost_micros":0,"downside":2,"delay":1} and a score. Idempotently re-POST a well-formed body over it so the response describes the STORED record. The response must show components.pSuccess === null and expected_contribution_micros === null. Repeat for opp_qa_ovf2_015 with pSuccess -1 and cost_micros 1. Capture the raw body — a jq projection that drops nulls will make a null look like an absent key and will make this check meaningless.

AC-14 PLANT AND READ: insert opp_qa_fitnull_020 for tenant_demo with the fit key DELETED from the stored record and every other component valid (value_micros 3000000000, pSuccess 0.5, cost_micros 1000000, infoValue 1, reversibility 0.9, downside 2, delay 1). Re-POST a well-formed body over it. The response must show components.fit === null AND expected_contribution_micros === 1499000000 AND the other seven components non-null. This is the direction the previous round's contract comment got backwards and the one the report did not file; check it explicitly.

AC-13/AC-14 TOGETHER, as a table rather than two cases: for every corrupt fixture planted above plus a healthy seeded row, the response must satisfy (expected_contribution_micros === null) === (components.value_micros === null OR components.pSuccess === null OR components.cost_micros === null). Report each fixture's verdict, and record the raw body for any that disagree. A build that satisfies only the first half of this is the failure this round is about.

AC-2/AC-9/AC-17 KEY SHAPE: for the same fixtures, confirm every response body carries all eight component keys with none dropped, and confirm the key order is value_micros, pSuccess, fit, infoValue, reversibility, cost_micros, downside, delay. Order is a wire-visible property and a rule table written in the wrong key order is a silent way to break it.

AC-15/AC-16 BROWSER: load /opportunities with the out-of-range records planted (pSuccess 1.5 and downside -1) and read the data-component spans for those rows: they must read 'success probability —' and 'downside —'. Confirm the healthy seeded row still reads 'success probability 0.6', 'fit 0.9' and 'downside 2', and that value and cost still render grouped with the rupee sign. Sweep every page and every state for 5xx, console errors, NaN, Infinity and the literal string 'undefined', as in previous rounds.

AC-8 INVARIANCE: diff the healthy seeded rows' projections against the pre-change build. Every seeded component value must be identical and none nulled. This is the check that the widened read rule did not start hiding values the domain accepts.
CLEANUP: delete every record planted by this run, and note in the report that experiment_evaluations is append-only by design and cannot be cleaned, as in previous rounds.

alternatives_considered.approach: Comment only — QA's hint, that the cheapest correct fix is to correct the CONTRACT comment and make no behaviour change.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not make the stated claim true, in either direction. The comment asserts a biconditional; QA filed one falsifying instance and I reproduced a second (a null fit beside a numeric contribution) that the comment's 'exactly when' also forbids. Correcting the prose to a one-direction claim was QA's own suggestion and that claim is refuted by the fit fixture. Shipping it would leave a comment that is still false and would burn the next QA run, which has no memory of this one, to rediscover it.

alternatives_considered.approach: State the contract in one direction only, as QA suggested: 'contribution is null whenever a component is null'.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Demonstrably false on the branch this work order replaces. A stored record with fit deleted returns components.fit === null and expected_contribution_micros 1499000000 over real HTTP. The formula reads three components, not eight, so no one-direction phrasing over all eight can hold. This is the clearest evidence that the defect is the comment's coupling, not a missing word in it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fold the overflowing product into the guard — QA's other option, reporting an unrepresentable product the same way as an unreadable component, so the projection nulls whichever component caused it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes a single key's readability depend on a combination of keys, so 'is this component readable' stops being a function of that component. That destroys the property attempt 2 correctly established and AC-12 states, re-creates a local rule inside the projection, and leaves the contract resting on a non-local predicate that is much harder to state correctly than the one being fixed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a wire flag, e.g. expected_contribution_unrepresentable: true, so the body says why the contribution is null.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: New public surface for a two-word overclaim, with no spec or PRD change behind it, and every client then has to handle two different ways of saying 'unknown'. The domain already has a way to say it: report the component the build cannot vouch for as null. That is the answer this build has given all along.

alternatives_considered.approach: Return 0 from expectedContribution on an unrepresentable product — attempt 1's behaviour.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Reintroduces exactly the sentinel collision this ticket exists to remove: a break-even bet legitimately contributes 0, so 0 cannot distinguish 'unknown' from 'genuinely nothing'. AC-1 forbids it explicitly and there is a standing test for it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Widen only pSuccess to its [0,1] range, leaving fit, reversibility, downside and delay on the looser number check.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A partial fix that adds a special case for one key — the exact shape of the duplication attempt 2 removed, and it would be reintroduced by this ticket rather than by the one that created it. It also leaves the read side accepting a fit of 2 and a downside of -1, which the seed guard would then have to treat differently from the API, and the seed's operator-facing message would be wrong for six of the eight keys.

alternatives_considered.approach: Re-validate the whole record on the read path by calling validateOpportunity and nulling every component when it fails.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: All-or-nothing, and it loses information the current design keeps: a record with one bad component would report all eight as null instead of naming the one that is wrong, which is the thing the seed's error message and AC-11 depend on. The per-key table gets the same protection with none of the loss.

assumptions: The stored score column is left alone. A record whose components now project with a null can still carry a non-null stored score, because the score is read from the column and is never recomputed on the read path. That is pre-existing — a pre-rename row already had a score — and no comment claims the score agrees with the components, so this change neither creates nor worsens it.

A stored value outside the domain's range is reachable only by writing to the database directly; every write path runs validateOpportunity. So widening the read rule cannot change what a legitimate client posted, only what a tampered row reads back as.

MONEY_COMPONENTS stays exported-internal and still drives validateOpportunity's OPP_BAD_MONEY code selection; the new table is a predicate table, not a code-selection table, and the two concerns are not merged.
unknowns: Whether a future QA run will file the raw `record` field, which stays unprojected and unfiltered on the repository result. The previous agent flagged this and it is still true; this change neither helps nor hurts it, because record is the stored JSON and the contract comment is about components.

Whether any consumer outside this repository reads expected_contribution_micros. The contract comment is the only published statement of it and there is no spec, PRD or TRD line for it — I grepped docs/ and the only hit is an unrelated metric name in the spec's data model.
risks: This work order deliberately reverses a boundary the previous attempt documented and pinned with a named test. If a reviewer disagrees with that judgement the right response is to reject this revision, not to run QA on it: the two positions cannot both be implemented, and the argument for this one is that a readable pSuccess of 1.5 is precisely what leaves the contribution unrepresentable.

The seed's exit code changes for a strictly larger set of databases than before. A database holding an out-of-range component that previously seeded as a clean no-op will now exit non-zero. This is the intent and matches AC-6 and AC-8, but anything invoking `npm run sdlc:seed` from CI or a dev script will start failing on such a database, and the message is the operator's only guidance — which is why the message text is in scope rather than left to drift.

The rule table must be written in COMPONENTS order. Deriving COMPONENTS from Object.keys of the table reorders the wire projection; I hit this while prototyping and the readability test caught it. If the implementer's version of the table is ordered differently, the projection's key order changes on the wire with no test failure outside the readability file.

Widening the read rule touches every consumer at once, so a mistake in the table is visible in the API, the page and the seed simultaneously. The per-key delegation table in AC-17 is the mitigation and is the first thing to look at if any of the three misbehaves.

A client that today reads a stored out-of-range value off the wire will now read null instead. Only reachable through direct database writes, so no legitimate client is affected, but it is a wire behaviour change and belongs in the PR body.
out_of_scope: The raw `record` field on repository results, which stays unprojected and unfiltered, as the previous attempt left it.
The stored score, which stays the sole rank key and is never recomputed or nulled on the read path.
Re-deriving the wire contract for any other endpoint; this contract exists only on POST /v1/opportunities.
docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md and docs/ui.md, which this change must not touch. No approved document states a contribution contract, so nothing there needs to change and nothing there may.
src/data/repositories.js and src/web/pages.js, which need no edit: the repository already projects through the shared rule and the page already renders the em-dash for a null component.
residual_risks: The raw `record` field is still returned alongside the projection, unfiltered. A client reading `record` rather than `components` still sees the stored float, string or out-of-range value. This is deliberate — record is the stored JSON and the previous attempt left it — but it is the one remaining path by which an untrustworthy number reaches a client, and QA is right to read it as such.

The contract comment is now true, and a comment is documentation rather than enforcement. The thing that keeps it true is the biconditional assertion in the route-level and domain-level tests, so those assertions are load-bearing and must not be relaxed to a spot check of the two QA shapes.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Both defects were reproduced, not inferred. I extracted the PR branch at a13c51f, started the app, planted the QA report's own fixtures over real HTTP and read the raw response bodies: opp_qa_ovf_014 returns all eight components non-null with expected_contribution_micros null, which is BUG-1 as filed. I then planted a record missing only fit and read components.fit null beside expected_contribution_micros 1499000000, the second falsifying instance QA did not file and the one that makes QA's own suggested fix wrong. I then prototyped the fix on the branch, measured its blast radius by running the suite (254 of 256 green; the only two failures are the two assertions that pin the boundary this work order overturns, and every API, page, seed, validation-code and message test is unaffected), and confirmed the corrected wire over HTTP for both fixtures, the em-dash render on /opportunities for two different keys, and the seed throwing OPP_STALE_RECORD on an out-of-range component. I also confirmed AC-8 holds — a healthy seeded row projects identically — and caught one real defect in my own prototype, that deriving COMPONENTS from the rule table reorders the wire, which is now called out in risks and pinned by AC-17. What keeps it off the high 90s: the central judgement is a reversal of a decision the previous attempt documented and tested on purpose, and a reasonable reviewer could reject it on those grounds, which is the correct outcome to reach before QA rather than after. The message wording is the implementer's to choose, within the constraint that it describe the rule it enforces.

history.action: route plan -> implement -> review -> qa (model, confidence 85)

review.title: The read-side and write-side rules are not one rule. validateOpportunity delegates its four per-key range/money loops to isReadableComponent, but keeps a fifth, whole-record check that the read side has no twin for: `!Number.isFinite(numeratorProduct(input))`. So a value can be readable on the way out while the domain would reject it on the way in, which is exactly the 'one definition of valid' bicondical AC-17 asserts. infoValue is the only unbounded multiplier in numeratorProduct, so it is the one key where the gap is reachable.
review.detail:
The read-side and write-side rules are not one rule. validateOpportunity delegates its four per-key range/money loops to isReadableComponent, but keeps a fifth, whole-record check that the read side has no twin for: `!Number.isFinite(numeratorProduct(input))`. So a value can be readable on the way out while the domain would reject it on the way in, which is exactly the 'one definition of valid' bicondical AC-17 asserts. infoValue is the only unbounded multiplier in numeratorProduct, so it is the one key where the gap is reachable.

`src/domain/opportunities.js:214`

Evidence: On PR head d830b29, for a record with value_micros 6e9, pSuccess 0.6, fit 0.9, reversibility 0.9, cost_micros 1.9e9, downside 2, delay 1 and infoValue swept:
  infoValue 1e+290  readable=true  validate=ACCEPT
  infoValue 5e+298  readable=true  validate=ACCEPT
  infoValue 5.6e+298 readable=true  validate=OPP_BAD_COMPONENT / components: the product of value_micros, pSuccess, fit, infoValue and reversibility must be a finite number
  infoValue 1e+300  readable=true  validate=OPP_BAD_COMPONENT (same)
  infoValue 1e+308  readable=true  validate=OPP_BAD_COMPONENT (same)
The threshold is record-dependent (product of the other four ~3.24e9, so anything above ~5.5e298).
Consequences on the shipped paths, both reproduced end to end:
1) Seed. Plant infoValue 1e308 into a fresh opp_seed_expensive and re-seed: `node scripts/seed.js` prints 'seed: tenant tenant_demo already present, nothing new written' and exits 0. The OPP_STALE_RECORD guard at scripts/seed.js:332 does not fire, because isReadableOpportunityRecord returns true. That is the AC-6 guarantee ('seeding a database that holds a record this build cannot read fails loudly ... instead of reporting a successful no-op') failing for this one key.
2) Wire. GET the same row through the repository: components = {"value_micros":6000000000,"pSuccess":0.6,"fit":0.9,"infoValue":1e+308,"reversibility":0.9,"cost_micros":1900000000,"downside":2,"delay":1}, score 0.9208. Eight non-null components, a number the domain could never have accepted, presented as trustworthy.
This is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced here: at base df0b3cd `isReadableComponent('infoValue', 1e308)` is also true and validateOpportunity also rejects. What the PR changes is that the claim moves from aspiration to asserted invariant -- the new test at test/domain/opportunities.test.js:197 is titled 'validateOpportunity and isReadableComponent are ONE rule, not two that agree today', and its per-key value lists (accepted/refused) contain no value anywhere near 1e299, so it does not exercise the one case where the two disagree.

Fix: Either close the gap or narrow the claim. To close it: give the read side the same whole-record constraint, e.g. have isReadableOpportunityRecord / readableComponents also require Number.isFinite(numeratorProduct(projection)) so an unrepresentable product nulls the key that caused it (infoValue), and add the ~5.6e298 case to the ONE-rule table. To narrow it: say in the comment at src/domain/opportunities.js:100 and in AC-17's test title that the shared predicate is a PER-KEY rule and that the whole-record product check on write has deliberately no read-side twin, and name who owns closing it.

review.title: `COMPONENT_RULES[key]?.(value) === true` looks up the rule on a plain object literal, so it walks Object.prototype. A key with no rule of its own is therefore not unreadable, which falsifies the doc comment directly above it ('so a key with no rule is unreadable rather than readable') and inverts AC-17's 'a component key cannot be added to the projection without a rule behind it' -- here a key with no rule behind it can be readable. One inherited key throws rather than answering.
review.detail:
`COMPONENT_RULES[key]?.(value) === true` looks up the rule on a plain object literal, so it walks Object.prototype. A key with no rule of its own is therefore not unreadable, which falsifies the doc comment directly above it ('so a key with no rule is unreadable rather than readable') and inverts AC-17's 'a component key cannot be added to the projection without a rule behind it' -- here a key with no rule behind it can be readable. One inherited key throws rather than answering.

`src/domain/opportunities.js:120`

Evidence: On PR head d830b29:
  isReadableComponent('hasOwnProperty', 'value_micros')    === true   (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty is callable and returns a boolean)
  isReadableComponent('propertyIsEnumerable', 'pSuccess')  === true
  isReadableComponent('__proto__', 1)                     throws TypeError: COMPONENT_RULES[key] is not a function
Latent only: every real caller passes a literal key or iterates COMPONENTS (src/domain/opportunities.js:130, :155, :190, :194, :200, :205, :278-280; src/web/pages.js:213), so no stored or wire-supplied key reaches this today. Reported because the two claims the code documents about itself are currently false, not because a reachable path exists.

Fix: Make the table prototype-free or the lookup own-property-only: `const COMPONENT_RULES = Object.assign(Object.create(null), {...})`, or `return Object.hasOwn(COMPONENT_RULES, key) && COMPONENT_RULES[key](value) === true;` and keep COMPONENTS as the separate ordered list it already is.

review.title: The OPP_STALE_RECORD guard is inside the per-candidate loop over the three fixed SEED_OPPORTUNITIES, so it can only ever see a record whose id is one of those three. An unreadable stored opportunity under any other id re-seeds as a clean exit-0 no-op, which is the AC-6 failure mode for every row the seed did not itself write.
review.detail:
The OPP_STALE_RECORD guard is inside the per-candidate loop over the three fixed SEED_OPPORTUNITIES, so it can only ever see a record whose id is one of those three. An unreadable stored opportunity under any other id re-seeds as a clean exit-0 no-op, which is the AC-6 failure mode for every row the seed did not itself write.

`scripts/seed.js:332`

Evidence: On PR head d830b29: seed a fresh DB, then INSERT a row with opportunity_id 'opp_not_a_seed' and record pSuccess 1.5 (all other components valid), then re-run `DB_PATH=... node scripts/seed.js`. Output: 'seed: tenant tenant_demo already present, nothing new written', exit 0. No OPP_STALE_RECORD. The two only writers of the opportunities table are src/api/routes.js:353 (which runs validateOpportunity) and scripts/seed.js:347, so the shape needs an out-of-band write -- the same reachability the other findings have. This matches AC-11's narrower wording ('a stored SEED record') and is consistent with the work order's design, so it is a scope observation rather than a regression.

Fix: Either widen the guard to a scan over repositories.opportunities.list(TENANT.id) for any unreadable record, or state the seed-id scope explicitly in the OPP_STALE_RECORD message and in the work order so AC-6's broader phrasing is not read as covering non-seed rows.

review.title: The single money renderer guards with isReadableComponent('value_micros', micros) for every amount it is handed, including cost_micros at line 694 and the non-opportunity amounts (ad-set budgets, insight spend, qualified CPL, experiment caps). It is correct today only because COMPONENT_RULES happens to map value_micros and cost_micros to the same function; the moment those two rules diverge, the view would keep applying value_micros's rule to cost_micros and to ad spend -- the class of per-consumer re-derivation AC-12 and AC-17 exist to stop.

`src/web/pages.js:213`

Evidence: src/web/pages.js:212-213 is the only money renderer in the file (grep 'function money' -> one hit). Its call sites: :191 row.daily_budget_micros, :193 row.spend_micros, :384 cpl, :694 the MONEY_COMPONENTS branch of opportunityRow (which covers cost_micros as well as value_micros), :772 caps.max_spend_micros and caps.max_downside_micros. Today isReadableComponent('value_micros', x) and isReadableComponent('cost_micros', x) return the same verdict for every input because src/domain/opportunities.js:90 and :95 name the same predicate, so no observable divergence exists. src/web/pages.js is listed in the work order's out_of_scope and this line predates the diff under review (it is already in df0b3cd), so this is an inherited coupling, not something this round introduced.

Fix: Thread the component key into money() -- money(raw, currency, key) defaulting to 'value_micros' -- and pass `key` at the opportunityRow:694 call site, so a future divergence between the two money rules is visible in the diff rather than silently absorbed.

review.detail:
The PR body's '## Changed' section is attempt 1's diffstat, not this branch's. Every count in it matches commit f3043db exactly and none matches the branch: it understates src/domain/opportunities.js by 6x (+24/-6 stated against +153/-17 actual) and src/api/routes.js by 4x (+5 against +19), overstates nothing, and omits test/domain/opportunity-readability.test.js (+297) entirely — the file attempt 2 created and the one that holds this ticket's cross-consumer theorem. Attempts 2 (a13c51f, +601) and 3 (2054855, +541) are not represented at all. A reviewer or QA sizing this review from that section counts 9 files and ~600 lines against a real 10 files and 1669 lines, and never learns a new test file exists.

`work-order.json:1`

Evidence: Commit f3043db (git show --stat): scripts/seed.js 30 changed, src/api/routes.js +5, src/data/repositories.js 11, src/domain/opportunities.js 30, src/web/pages.js 70, test/api/opportunities.test.js +142, test/domain/opportunities.test.js 61, test/ops/seed.test.js +173, test/web/pages.test.js 134. The PR body lists exactly 29/-1, 5/-0, 9/-2, 24/-6, 44/-26, 142/-0, 52/-9, 173/-0, 127/-7 — a line-for-line match, and no other commit on the branch matches. Branch reality: git log --oneline 602444f..d830b29 is f3043db, a13c51f, 2054855 plus framework merges; gh pr view 43 --json files reports opportunities.js 153/17, routes.js 19/0, opportunity-readability.test.js 297/0 ADDED.

Fix: Regenerate the section from `gh pr view 43 --json files` rather than by hand, and add one line naming the three commits this branch carries for issue #40 (f3043db, a13c51f, 2054855) and stating that the current work order governs only the third. The council and QA both read that body as the description of what to review, so it should be right before either runs. Separate note for the pipeline, not the implementer: the work order's own files[]/out_of_scope name only 3 source files, and this round's commit 2054855 touches exactly those 3 plus the 5 files in tests[] — so src/web/pages.js and src/data/repositories.js appearing in `gh pr diff 43` are attempts 1 and 2 of this same issue, not scope creep, and must not be reverted or re-litigated on the strength of the work order's out_of_scope note alone.
